info.title: 2dog
info.description: 2dog command-line tool and project templates. `dnx 2dog new MyGame` interactively creates a Godot project with .NET hosts; `2dog add` adds hosts (desktop, browser-wasm, xUnit, WinForms, WinUI 3, Avalonia, Blazor) to an existing one; every prompt has a flag, so `2dog new MyGame --desktop --tests` runs unattended. `2dog doctor` checks the project and the machine, applies safe fixes and explains build failures; `2dog update` brings the 2dog packages to the tool's versions. `2dog pack list` inspects an exported .pck. `dotnet new install 2dog` provides the `dotnet new 2dog` project template. The engine library itself is the 2dog.engine package.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not prompt; take the flags and defaults (also --non-interactive, --no-input) [default: False]

options.name: --version
options.description: Print tool and package versions; under dnx use '2dog version' (dnx consumes --version itself; to pin the tool version: 'dnx 2dog@<version>') [default: False]

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help; after a verb, the help for that verb [default: False]

options.name: --json
options.description: Machine-readable output: one JSON document on stdout, nothing else; implies --yes [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Results and problems only: no header, plan, progress or next steps [default: False]

options.name: --plain
options.description: No colour, no cursor movement, ASCII markers (also TERM=dumb) [default: False]

options.name: --no-color
options.description: No colour (also the NO_COLOR environment variable) [default: False]

options.name: --accessible
options.description: Screen-reader friendly: numbered yes/no questions instead of lists, no spinners (also TWODOG_ACCESSIBLE=1) [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Extra detail on stderr: subprocess command lines and their output, stack traces [default: False]

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a new Godot project with 2dog hosts

options.name: --name
options.description: Project name (new) or base name override (names are reduced to letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'; adjustments are announced)

options.name: --output
options.description: Directory for a new project

options.name: --desktop
options.description: Desktop host (your own Main entry point)

options.description: WinForms host embedding the game window (Windows-only; never part of the default set)

options.name: --winui
options.description: WinUI 3 host embedding the game window (Windows-only, like --winforms; builds only on Windows)

options.name: --avalonia
options.description: Avalonia host embedding the game in a cross-platform GUI (opt-in, like --winforms)

options.name: --blazor
options.description: Blazor Web App host: ASP.NET Core server plus a WebAssembly client page embedding the game (opt-in; needs wasm-tools)

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check the project and this machine, fix what can be fixed

options.name: --fix
options.description: Apply the safe fixes, then check again [default: False]

options.name: --fix-all
options.description: Also apply the announced fixes (solution migration, target framework, bootstrap refresh) [default: False]

options.name: --ignore
options.description: Drop a finding by id (repeatable; --list-checks shows the ids)

options.name: --strict
options.description: Warnings count as findings for the exit code [default: False]

options.name: --list-checks
options.description: List every check and build-log signature [default: False]
